To survive at-least-once delivery, an append-only event log requires its writers to be idempotent, not safe, because appending to the log is inherently a side effect.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the log does not support deduplication via unique IDs, the writers cannot guarantee idempotency, and at-least-once delivery would lead to duplicate logs.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the system relies on a non-standard definition of 'safe', the distinction may not hold.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If a writer sends an append request and it times out, at-least-once delivery guarantees the writer will retry. If the operation is safe (no side effects), it couldn't append to the log at all. If it is idempotent, the log can identify the duplicate request via a unique event ID and ignore subsequent duplicates, ensuring the log's state is identical to the state if it had been appended exactly once.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
